name: Samsun
title: Samsun UTM | Ship Thickness Measurement, Black Sea Coast
description: Ship thickness measurement in Samsun for general cargo ships, bulkers, ro-ro and coasters at the port or anchorage: hull, hatch covers, tanks and deck piping.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Samsun for Black Sea Cargo Ships
intro: Samsun is the main port of the central Black Sea coast of Turkey, handling general cargo, grain, steel, fertiliser, containers and ro-ro traffic for Anatolia's interior and for transit trade across the Black Sea. It sees a steady procession of coasters, bulkers and multipurpose ships. Atlantis technicians travel from India to the ship, and the gauging is arranged around berth stays, cargo sequences and the anchorage waits that come with a busy roadstead.
keywords: black sea general cargo ship inspection

highlights.p: Grain and fertiliser bulkers, steel carriers, container feeders and ro-ro ships all call here. A single mobilisation can meet different ship types, each with its own typical wear pattern and gauging scope.

highlights.h: Cargo stays long enough to work
highlights.p: Bulk and general cargo calls at Samsun usually last long enough to open holds in sequence, take ballast tank readings and measure hatch covers, without disturbing the cargo programme.

highlights.h: Gauging ahead of a docking elsewhere
highlights.p: With no major ocean-going drydock on this stretch of coast, readings taken at Samsun give owners a measured scope before they send a ship to the Marmara or abroad for steel work.

port.h: Samsun: gateway of the central Black Sea coast
p: Samsun lies on the Black Sea coast of Turkey, at the northern end of the road and rail links into central Anatolia, and its port is the largest on this part of the coast. Berths handle general cargo, bulk, containers and ro-ro traffic, and the port acts as a transit point for goods moving to and from the interior and across the sea to other Black Sea countries. The approach is open to the north, with breakwaters protecting the berths, and weather in winter can disrupt berthing and anchorage work for days at a time.

The cargo mix is varied. Grain and agricultural products, fertiliser and minerals arrive and leave in Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers and in coasters. Steel and project cargo move in general cargo and multipurpose ships, while container feeders and ro-ro vessels serve regional trades. Many ships here are operated by Turkish and Black Sea owners who keep older tonnage trading, so structural condition varies widely. Ro-ro ships bring a different set of concerns, including car deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks, and general cargo ships bring hatch covers and coaming structure into the picture.

Anchorage waiting is a regular feature when berths are busy or when the weather shuts the port. Ships may lie off the port for a day or several, giving time for deck and ballast tank work if conditions permit. The inspection pattern at Samsun mirrors the rest of the Turkish Black Sea: owners want to know the condition of holds and hatch covers, charterers ask for evidence at delivery, and buyers of second-hand tonnage want readings before concluding a sale. Because major dockings happen elsewhere, Samsun is chiefly a place for preparing and informing a docking rather than for carrying it out.

At the port, ships are gauged alongside during cargo work. Holds are opened one by one as discharge finishes, ballast tanks are measured when they are empty and ventilated, and hatch covers and coamings are checked from the deck. Container feeders offer shorter windows, in which we limit the scope to a defined set of tanks or to scrubber and ballast piping. Access is through the terminal's security procedures and is arranged through the ship's agent, with crew prepared to issue entry permits and have spaces gas-free before we board.

For ships at anchor, launches are booked by the agent and the sea state decides what is feasible. The work is ordered so that the most valuable readings come first, usually ballast tanks and deck plating at hatch corners, and any remaining scope is picked up at the next call or in dock. Ships that will dock in the Marmara or in a yard elsewhere are given their readings organised by frame and strake, so the yard can use them for ordering steel before the ship arrives.
list: Samsun port general cargo and bulk berths — hold, hatch cover and coaming gauging as cargo work releases each space
Container and multipurpose berths — short-window checks of ballast tanks, deck structure and piping on feeders and project ships
Ro-ro berths — car deck plating, ramp structure and ballast tank gauging on ro-ro ships during turnaround calls
Anchorage off the port — deck and ballast tank gauging on ships waiting for a berth or weather, by launch via the agent
Pre-docking and pre-purchase gauging — an organised steel scope handed to the superintendent or the buyer's adviser before decisions are made

context.h: Regulation and trade on the central Black Sea coast
p: Ship safety and port operations in Turkey sit with the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure and the harbour masters, and Turkish ports are covered by both the Black Sea MoU and the Mediterranean MoU on port state control. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships on regional trades are inspected often, and the findings that tend to recur are structural: wasted hatch covers, corroded coamings, holed ventilators and degraded air pipe heads. A deficiency at Samsun or a neighbouring port is a common reason for an owner to commission gauging of the surrounding steel.

Because the Black Sea is outside the emission control areas, ships here follow the global fuel limit unless they have come from or are heading to the Marmara or Mediterranean. Trade from Samsun links Turkey with Ukraine, Russia, Georgia and Romania, and shipping on these routes is shaped by the wider regional situation, which makes schedules less predictable than usual. For vessels that call at EU ports, the EU Ship Recycling Regulation's Inventory of Hazardous Materials and EU ETS reporting add compliance work, but not extra steel measurement. Owners rely on readings to plan docking and to support charter negotiations.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Samsun
jobs.p: Jobs at Samsun reflect the cargo trades and the age of the regional fleet. Grain and fertiliser bulkers give hold access in sequence, general cargo ships give hatch and coaming work, ro-ro ships give car deck and ramp measurements, and ships at anchor give time for tanks. The work is usually ordered by a technical department preparing a docking or by a buyer assessing a ship.
list: Hold frame and tank-top gauging on a Supramax bulk carrier discharging grain, in preparation for a special survey in a Marmara yard.
Hatch cover, coaming and cross-deck gauging on a general cargo ship after port state control noted corroded coamings at a neighbouring Black Sea port.
Car deck plating, ramp and ballast tank readings on a ro-ro ship during a turnaround call at Samsun, sent to the superintendent before sailing.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a Handysize bulker at anchor, with the buyer's adviser attending and readings reported before the sale proceeded.
Deck piping and ballast line wall-thickness checks on a coaster during a short cargo stay, to decide which sections to renew at the next docking.

logistics: Samsun has its own regional airport, and the team normally connects through Istanbul to reach it. From the airport the port is reached by road, and the agent handles gate passes, terminal safety briefings and anchorage launches, with crew lists and certificates sent ahead. A Turkish visa is required for Indian passport holders, so we start the application when a call looks likely and keep the validity wide enough to cover delays in the ship's schedule or weather holds at the port.

faqs.q: Can ro-ro ships be gauged during a turnaround call?
faqs.a: Yes, within the window available. The usual targets are car deck plating, ramp and door structure, and ballast tanks that the crew have emptied and ventilated beforehand. Spaces in use for cargo are left alone. We agree the list with the superintendent, measure the most important areas first and report each area as it is finished.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Samsun for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: No large ocean-going drydock operates on this stretch of coast. Owners generally dock in the Marmara region or at a yard abroad. Gauging at Samsun therefore concentrates on holds, hatch covers, tanks and deck, giving the owner a measured steel scope before the ship goes to dock.

faqs.q: What can be done at the anchorage off Samsun?
faqs.a: Launch access depends on sea state, but when it is workable we gauge deck plating, hatch covers, coamings and ballast tanks that have been prepared by the crew. Holds that are empty and safe to enter can be measured as well. If the ship is called to berth, we finish what we can and report the remainder.

faqs.q: How are Black Sea schedule changes handled for a mobilisation?
faqs.a: We ask for a likely call window as early as possible and keep the Turkish visas valid across it. Flights are fixed once the agent confirms the berth or anchorage plan. If the ship is delayed, diverted or sails early, the plan changes, and we agree with the owner how any partly completed scope is reported.
